narrative:
The model estimates you have a 16% chance of not passing your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires additional support. This doesn’t mean failure is certain, but it does mean the system has identified patterns in your situation that often lead to difficulties, so you’ll need to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances.

The most reassuring factor is that you’ve never failed a class before—this is a strong positive sign and the main reason your risk isn’t even higher. However, two other key aspects are working against you. First, while you do plan to pursue higher education, this goal alone isn’t enough to offset other challenges. Second, your social life shows a moderate level of going out with friends, which the model associates with slightly higher risk, possibly because it can distract from study time.

Other details in your profile also played a role, though less strongly. For example, your free time after school is lower than most students, which may limit opportunities to catch up on work. Your family relationships are described as fair rather than good or very good, and your parents’ education levels are below the average of students who pass without extra help. On the positive side, you’ve had no absences, and your alcohol consumption is very low, both of which support your success.

The remedial courses are an opportunity to focus on areas where the model sees potential risk. Use this time to create a consistent study routine, seek extra help if needed, and balance your social life with your academic goals. The system believes in your potential—this is your chance to prove it.
